new.title: Stand at the Wasserkunst on Wismar's market square
new.desc: Wismar's Marktplatz is one of the largest medieval squares on the German Baltic coast, at the heart of the old town that became UNESCO World Heritage with Stralsund in 2002. The Wasserkunst, a Dutch-Renaissance pavilion of 1602, supplied the town with drinking water until 1897.
new.tip: Free to wander at any hour; the square is quietest early in the morning and lit up in the evening.

new.title: Look up inside the giant brick nave of St. Nikolai
new.desc: St. Nikolai, built 1381 to 1487, was the church of Wismar's seafarers and fishermen. Its brick vault rises about 37 metres, among the highest of Brick Gothic, and the tower was lost in a storm in 1703.
new.tip: Open daily for visitors; a small donation is welcome. Combine with the nearby Alter Hafen.

new.title: Ride the lift up St. Georgen for a view over Wismar
new.desc: St. Georgen, the largest of Wismar's three big brick churches, was destroyed in 1945 and rebuilt over decades, finished in 2010. A lift takes visitors to a viewing platform over the roofs, the harbour and the Bay of Wismar.
new.tip: The platform costs a few euros; check seasonal hours on wismar.de. Best on a clear afternoon.

new.title: Admire the Renaissance terracotta of the Fürstenhof
new.desc: Built 1512 to 1513 for Duke Heinrich V and Duke Albrecht VII of Mecklenburg, the Fürstenhof is a north German showpiece of Italian Renaissance ornament in terracotta. It later served as an administrative building and today houses the court.
new.tip: Look at the street facade on Lübsche Straße; the building is not a museum.

new.title: Explore Wismar's history in the Schabbellhaus
new.desc: The Schabbell Museum of city history occupies the Renaissance Schabbellhaus of 1569, with a modern extension. Exhibits cover Wismar's Hanseatic past, the Swedish rule from 1648 and maritime trade.
new.tip: Closed Mondays; hours differ between listings, so check wismar.de/schabbell before going.

new.title: Walk the Baroque park of Schloss Bothmer in Klütz
new.desc: Schloss Bothmer, built from 1726 for Count Hans Caspar von Bothmer, is the largest Baroque palace in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. Its museum and the surrounding English landscape park are open to visitors.
new.tip: The park is open daily year-round; in winter the museum opens only at weekends, so check before going.

new.title: Tour Schloss Ludwigslust, the Versailles of the north
new.desc: From 1772 to 1776 Duke Friedrich built this neo-Baroque palace as the residence of the Mecklenburg-Schwerin court. Much of the rich interior decoration is papier-mâché, cast as a cheaper substitute for stone and stucco.
new.tip: Check museum days before going; the palace park is free and open all day.

new.title: Walk the walls of the Dömitz fortress on the Elbe
new.desc: The Festung Dömitz is a Renaissance fortress of 1559 to 1565 on the Elbe. Fritz Reuter was imprisoned here from 1837 to 1840, and the complex today hosts exhibitions and open-air events.
new.tip: Check seasonal opening times; courtyard concerts run in summer.

new.title: Visit St. Georgen, Parchim's brick town church
new.desc: St. Georgen is the large Gothic brick church of Parchim's old town on the Elde, begun in the 13th century and enlarged in the 14th. It stands near the old town wall.
new.tip: Opening days vary; ask at the tourist office. Combine with a walk along the Elde.

new.title: Step into Sternberg's Stadtkirche and its Heilig-Blut legend
new.desc: The Stadtkirche in Sternberg is a Brick Gothic hall church. In 1492 the town was the scene of a Host desecration trial against Jews that ended in executions and made it a pilgrimage site until the Reformation.
new.tip: Open in summer; ask at the museum nearby for entry.

new.title: Watch the Hubbrücke lift over the Elde in Plau am See
new.desc: The Plauer Hubbrücke is a steel lift bridge over the Elde, first built in 1916 and rebuilt in 1999. The deck rises for boat traffic into Plauer See and gives a good view of the town waterfront.
new.tip: Free. Combine with a walk past the Burgturm and the Elde harbour.
new.q: Hubbrücke, Quetziner Straße, 19395 Plau am See

new.title: Meet the Roland of Perleberg before the town hall
new.desc: The Roland statue of 1546 stands before the late-Gothic town hall on Perleberg's market. It is one of the largest Rolands in Germany at about 5.5 metres, and symbolises the town's market and judicial rights.
new.tip: Free outdoors; the St. Jakobi church is a short stroll away.

new.title: Visit the Wunderblutkirche St. Nikolai in Bad Wilsnack
new.desc: After a fire in 1383 three blood-stained communion wafers were said to be found in the ruins, making Wilsnack one of the biggest pilgrimage destinations of northern Europe. The Gothic hall church built for the pilgrims still stands, and the pilgrim trail from Berlin ends here.
new.tip: Open for visitors in daytime; ask at the church about tours.
new.q: Wunderblutkirche St. Nikolai, Kirchplatz, 19336 Bad Wilsnack

new.title: Cross the moat to Plattenburg, a huge water castle
new.desc: Plattenburg in the Prignitz is one of the largest preserved moated castles in northern Germany, a medieval complex restored from the 1990s. It has an exhibition on its history, a courtyard and regular events.
new.tip: Check museum season and days on the castle website before driving out.

new.title: Visit the Waldemarturm above Dannenberg
new.desc: The Waldemarturm is the remaining tower of the medieval castle of Dannenberg, associated with Waldemar of Denmark. It stands on a hill above the Jeetzel in the middle of this Wendland town.
new.tip: The hill is free to visit; check the town museum for tower access.

new.title: Step into a Bronze Age longhouse at Hitzacker
new.desc: The Archäologisches Zentrum Hitzacker is an open-air museum built near a prehistoric settlement found in 1969. It includes three reconstructed Bronze Age longhouses and demonstrations of ancient crafts.
new.tip: Open daily from April to October, 10:00 to 17:00; closed in winter.

new.title: See the Wiligrad Maschinenhaus and castle grounds
new.desc: Schloss Wiligrad on the Schweriner See was built 1896 to 1898 as a summer residence of Duke Johann Albrecht. Its facade is under renovation, and the Kunstverein Wiligrad runs exhibitions in the Maschinenhaus on site.
new.tip: The Maschinenhaus is open Tuesday to Sunday; check exhibition dates at kunstverein-wiligrad.de.

new.title: Drink house-brewed beer at Brauhaus am Lohberg in Wismar
new.desc: Brauhaus am Lohberg brews its own beers in Wismar's old town and serves regional dishes in a historic setting.
new.tip: Open from 11:00; try the house beer with a fish or Mecklenburg dish and book for evenings.
new.q: Brauhaus am Lohberg, Kleine Hohe Straße 15, 23966 Wismar

new.title: Eat a smoked-fish roll at the Hafenräucherei on Insel Poel
new.desc: The Hafenräucherei in Kirchdorf on Poel's harbour smokes fish in its own smokehouse and sells fish rolls, fries and its own liqueurs. It is a regular stop for cyclists on the Baltic route.
new.tip: Try a warm smoked fish roll; opening hours vary by season.
new.q: Hafenräucherei Kirchdorf, Am Hafen, 23999 Insel Poel

new.title: Have cake in the hunting hall of the Ludwigsluster Schlosscafé
new.desc: The Schlosscafé occupies the former Jagdsaal of the ducal palace and serves home-baked tortes and cakes with coffee. The terrace faces the park.
new.tip: Ask for the cake of the day; check opening, which follows the museum season.

new.title: Eat smoked lake fish at the Fischerhaus in Plau am See
new.desc: The Fischerhaus on the Metow is a fish restaurant with its own smokehouse, serving lake fish and regional specialities with a smoked-fish platter on the menu. It also runs smoking courses.
new.tip: Order the Räucherfischplatte; reserve in high season.
new.q: Fischerhaus Plau am See, An der Metow 14, 19395 Plau am See

new.title: Eat fish with a lake view at Seeschlösschen in Grevesmühlen
new.desc: The Seeschlösschen is a restaurant and café on the Ploggensee with fish and meat dishes, cake and its own smokehouse.
new.tip: Try the smoked fish plate, then walk the lakeshore.

new.title: Order the day's catch at Blinkfür in Boltenhagen
new.desc: Blinkfür is a fish restaurant that has served fresh Baltic fish since 1994, close to the Boltenhagen seafront.
new.tip: Open evenings from 17:30 and closed Mondays; ask for the fresh catch.

new.title: Have cake in the Orangerie café at Schloss Bothmer
new.desc: The Orangerie café at Schloss Bothmer serves home-made cakes and tortes plus savoury dishes beside the palace park.
new.tip: Sit in the courtyard in summer; check winter days.
new.q: Orangerie Schloss Bothmer, Börzower Weg 1, 23948 Klütz

new.title: Eat bakery cake at the Alter Speicher in Bad Wilsnack
new.desc: Alter Speicher am Bahndamm is a café and restaurant with its own bakery and a daily changing cake selection.
new.tip: Book ahead and ask for the cake of the day.
new.q: Alter Speicher am Bahndamm, Bahnhofstraße, 19336 Bad Wilsnack

new.title: Have breakfast at Café Anton near the Wittenberge harbour
new.desc: Café Anton is a small café near the Elbe harbour in Wittenberge, known for its breakfast.
new.tip: Go on a weekend morning; check opening days.

new.title: Eat cake at Markthof Satemin in a Rundling village
new.desc: Markthof Satemin is a country café in the round village of Satemin, with home-baked cake and burgers and seating facing the village green.
new.tip: Sit outside in good weather; check seasonal hours.

new.title: Have lunch at Café Albis in Hitzacker's old town
new.desc: Café Albis is a vegetarian-friendly café on the main street of Hitzacker's island old town, rated 4.5 on HappyCow.
new.tip: Try the daily soup or cake; check opening days.

new.title: Dine at Field in the Hotel Katerberg in Lüchow
new.desc: Field is the restaurant of Hotel Katerberg in Lüchow, run by chef Salvatore Fontanazza, serving modern European cooking with main courses around 35 to 45 euros.
new.tip: Book ahead for the evening; the top price level here.

new.title: Eat at the Klützer Mühle with its farm shop
new.desc: The Klützer Mühle serves traditional German cooking made with fresh ingredients and has a farm shop and café.
new.tip: Combine with a visit to nearby Schloss Bothmer.

new.title: Take a harbour cruise from Wismar's old harbour
new.desc: Boats leave the Alter Hafen for tours of the harbour and the Bay of Wismar. The old harbour with its Baumhaus lies in the UNESCO World Heritage area.
new.tip: Cruises run mainly April to October; check times on the quay.

new.title: Walk the Boltenhagen pier and swim off the long beach
new.desc: Boltenhagen has a beach of more than five kilometres, interrupted only by the 290-metre pier opened in 1992. The Kurpark adjoins the promenade.
new.tip: Swimming is best June to September; sunsets from the pier.

new.title: Swim at Timmendorf Strand on Insel Poel
new.desc: Timmendorf on Poel's north tip has a beach, a harbour and a lighthouse. The island connects to the mainland by a bridge from Wismar.
new.tip: Swimming June to September; cycle from Kirchdorf along the dyke.

new.title: Stroll the Ludwigslust palace park and its canals
new.desc: The landscape park with canals and cascades surrounds the palace and holds the Schweizerhaus and a grotto.
new.tip: Free; allow two hours for a loop.

new.title: Swim in the Plauer See at Plau am See
new.desc: Plau am See lies on the western shore of the Plauer See, one of Mecklenburg's largest lakes, and has a public bathing beach.
new.tip: Swimming June to September; combine with a boat trip.
new.q: Strandbad Plau am See, 19395 Plau am See

new.title: Cycle the Elbe flood-plain trail at Dömitz
new.desc: The Elberadweg passes Dömitz and the Elbe Biosphere Reserve, with views over river meadows.
new.tip: Spring and early summer for birdlife; flat riding.

new.title: Soak in brine at the Kristall Kur- und Gradier-Therme
new.desc: The Kristalltherme in Bad Wilsnack has indoor and outdoor brine pools, saunas and wellness treatments. The town has carried the title Bad since 1929.
new.tip: Check weekday hours and sauna days before arriving.
new.q: Kristall Kur- und Gradier-Therme, Am Kähling 1, 19336 Bad Wilsnack

new.title: Swim in the Crivitzer See
new.desc: Crivitz lies on the Crivitzer See, with a bathing spot at the lakeshore.
new.tip: Swimming June to September.

new.title: Hike the Sternberger Seenlandschaft lakes
new.desc: The Sternberger Seenlandschaft is a landscape of lakes and moraine hills around Sternberg, with marked hiking and cycling paths from the town.
new.tip: Spring or autumn; start from the lake behind the museum.

new.title: Swim in the Gartower See in the Elbtalaue
new.desc: The Gartower See near Gartow in the Wendland has a public bathing beach in the Niedersächsische Elbtalaue biosphere reserve.
new.tip: Swimming June to September.

new.title: Cross the Elbe on the Neu Darchau ferry
new.desc: The Neu Darchau to Darchau ferry is a car and bicycle ferry on the Elbe, a link on the Elberadweg.
new.tip: Check crossing times; there is no bridge for long stretches here.

new.title: Climb to the Veritas clock tower in Wittenberge
new.desc: The 1929 Uhrenturm of the former Veritas sewing-machine works carries one of Europe's largest tower clocks and is a landmark of the Prignitz town on the Elbe.
new.tip: Check tour dates with the town; the Elbe promenade is free.
